findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer in the sani bucket on the counter in the lobby was measured between 100-0 ppm. The PIC was Made aware. The sani bucket was remade and tested at 200 ppm. Ensure that sanitizer concentrations are monitored at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The caulking on the hand sink by the kitchen entrance was observed coming oof the wall. Discussed with the PIC. The PIC assured inspector that the sink will be repaired. Ensure that the caulking at this sink is repaired accordingly.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: The ventilation duct above the sandwich's station was observed with an accumulation of dust and soil. The PIC was made aware. Ensure that the vent duct is monitored, cleaned, and kept free of dust and soil at all times.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.14 Cleaning Ventilation Systems, Nuisance and Discharge Prohibition. (A) Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. (B) If vented to the outside, ventilation systems may not create a public health HAZARD or nuisance or unLAWful discharge.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed employee switching tasks during food preparation without washing their hands before donning gloves when returning to their previous food preparation task. Discussed with PIC with and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable to wash their hands when switching tasks during food preparation including before donning new gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There were no paper towels available at the hand sink next to the walk-in cooler in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC and paper towels were provided for the hand sink mentioned. Ensure that all hand sinks are supplied with the relevant materials to enable adequate handwashing at all times.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspector observed juice in a cardboard box being stored on the floor in the walk-in cooler. Discussed with PIC and paper towels the Box of juice was adequately stored. Ensure that food items are stored at least 6 inches above the floor to protect them from splash, dust and other contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed personal clothing being stored on the shelves in the walk-in cooler. Discussed with PIC and the clothing mentioned was removed to be stored in a designated area within the facility. Ensure that staff are aware to store their personal belongings in a designated area away from food items to avoid possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The shelves and the fans of the walk-in cooler are observed to be in need of a cleaning. Ensure that these areas are cleaned by the next routine inspection. Nonfood contact surfaces should be cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean. 

NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The pizza slicers at the start of the inspection were observed stored at the triple sink against the faucet with the food contact surface in contact with the sanitizer tubing, the pipe, and the handles. These items were removed form this location and placed on the drying rack. Ensure food contact surfaces of utensils are stored in a manner that prevents contamination.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: There is observed an accumulation of debris in the corner of the dry storage shelves in the kitchen. Ensure detailed cleaning is accomplished in hard to reach areas to remove and debris from the floor of the facility.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Observed deli meats such as turkey and bologna in the sandwich prep cooler that were not marked with the date of opening. There was also one tub of BBQ beef in the pizza prep cooler that was dated with an open date of 9/30--this exceeds the 7 days allowed. This was discussed with the manager. Date mark all ready to eat, time and temperature control for safety foods with the date of opening and hold no longer than 7 days maximum.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the collar in the drain pipe for the soda fountain machine to have soil accumulation in it. Clean this drain pipe.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.
